s: Which of the following is a plains tribe found in almost all plain districts of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Yerukula are a plains tribe; Konda Kapu and Manna Dhora live in the northern hill and frontier areas, and Kulia and Rona in the northern agency tracts.

s: Which of the following tribe–location pairs is correctly matched?
x: Gadaba live around Salur and Parvathipuram on the northern border; Koya belong to the Godavari valley, Jatapu to Srikakulam–Vizianagaram and Yanadi to the Nellore plains.

s: Kotia is associated with which of the following areas?
x: The Kotia live in the Visakhapatnam highlands of the northern agency. The Nallamala forests belong to the Chenchu, and the Nellore plains to the Yanadi.

s: The Yanadi tribe is associated with which area of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Yanadi live in the Nellore plains; Sugali (Lambadi, Banjara) are associated with Rayalaseema and central Andhra.

o: Bagata — Visakhapatnam and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts
Konda Reddi — Godavari banks and adjoining hills

s: Which of the following tribe–area pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Jatapu live in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram; the Chenchu are in the Nallamala forests, the Yanadi in the Nellore plains and the Koya in the Godavari valley.

s: Which of the following tribes is associated with podu cultivation in the hill tracts of East and West Godavari and is also a PVTG?
x: The Konda Reddis inhabit the hill tracts of East and West Godavari, particularly the Rampa region, practise podu cultivation and are classified as a PVTG.

s: The Konda Doras served as which of the following in the Rampa agency?
x: The Konda Doras served as Mutadars, or hill chiefs, of the Rampa agency.

s: Which tribe of Andhra Pradesh is associated with the Nallamala forests?
x: The Chenchu are the Nallamala tribe; Konda Dhora live in the northern Eastern Ghats, Kondh on the Odisha border, and Nakkala in plains and commercial areas.

s: Which tribe's name is traditionally taken to mean 'those who live under trees'?
x: Chenchu means 'those who live under trees'; their origin myth is the marriage of Ahobilam Narasimha with Chenchita.

s: Which of the following describes the Chenchus of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The earliest urban tribe of the coast
The aboriginal tribe of Andhra Pradesh
x: The Chenchus are described as the “aboriginal tribe” of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Bhil, like Munda and Santhal, is a tribe of other States, not a major tribe of Andhra Pradesh; Savara, Koya and Yanadi are AP tribes.

s: Which of the following is NOT a tribe of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Santhal, like Munda and Bhil, is not an AP tribe; Koya, Savara and Jatapu are.

s: Which tribe of Andhra Pradesh calls itself 'Koyi Toor'?
x: The Koyas of the Godavari basin call themselves Koyi Toor.

s: The Porja tribe of Andhra Pradesh mainly lives in which area?
x: Porja live in the Araku Valley of the Visakhapatnam agency.

s: Near which lake was the original home of the Yanadi tribe?
x: The Yanadis of the Nellore plains had their original home near Pulicat Lake.

s: The Yerukula tribe of Andhra Pradesh is known by which name in Tamil Nadu?
x: Yerukulas are called Korava in Tamil Nadu and Korcha in Karnataka.

s: According to tribal myth, which deity of Ahobilam married Chenchita, a Chenchu girl?
x: The Chenchu myth says Ahobilam Narasimha married Chenchita.

s: What are the traditional settlements of the Lambada (Sugali) community called?
x: Lambadas live in thandas; once traders and transporters, they now practise agriculture and animal husbandry.

s: How many Scheduled Tribes were counted in Census 2011?
x: Census 2011 counted 698, while more than 700 tribes are notified under Article 342, some overlapping more than one State.

s: The SC and ST Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976 notified how many Scheduled Tribes in undivided Andhra Pradesh?
x: The 1976 Act notified 33 STs, five with area restrictions (Gowdu, Mali, Nayak, Thoti, Valmiki); APSES 2024-25 counts 34 ST communities in present AP.

s: Which State has the largest number of notified Scheduled Tribes (62)?
x: Odisha has 62 notified tribes; under Article 342 the President notifies STs after consulting the Governor, and only Parliament can amend the list by law.

s: How many Scheduled Tribe communities does present Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Present AP has 34 ST communities; 33 is the 1976 Act figure for undivided AP and 698 the Census 2011 India count.

s: Under Article 342, who notifies the Scheduled Tribes of a State?
x: The President notifies STs after consulting the Governor; only Parliament can amend the list.

s: Which Article of the Constitution defines Scheduled Tribes?
x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes; Article 342 deals with their notification.

s: Which is the largest tribe of India?
x: The Bhil is India's largest tribe; it is not a tribe of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following communities are Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh only in the Agency Tracts?
x: Gowdu, Nayak and Valmiki are among the five area-restricted STs, recognised only in the Agency Tracts.

s: Who can amend the list of Scheduled Tribes notified under Article 342?
x: The President notifies STs after consulting the Governor, but only Parliament can amend the list.

s: In February 2024, sub-groups of which tribes were added to the Scheduled Tribe list of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Bondo Porja, Khond Porja and Konda Savara were added to AP's ST list in February 2024.

s: According to Census 2011, Scheduled Tribes formed what percentage of Andhra Pradesh's population?
x: AP has 27.39 lakh STs, 5.53 per cent of its population; about 12.9 lakh tribals live in Scheduled Areas.

s: Where is the headquarters of Polavaram district, carved out of Alluri Sitharama Raju district on 31 December 2025?

s: According to Census 2011, Scheduled Castes formed what share of Andhra Pradesh's population?

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest Scheduled Caste share in Census 2011?
x: Prakasam had the highest SC share (23.19%), followed by Nellore (22.49%).

s: Visakhapatnam district (now largely Alluri Sitarama Raju district) was first in Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011 for which population group?

x: PVTGs are identified by pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and a stagnant population; rapid population growth is not a criterion.

s: To which body was the Social Progress Index (December 2022) submitted?
o: Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister

s: Which of the following were the top three in Tier-I of the Social Progress Index 2022?

s: Which States topped the SDG India Index 2023-24 with a score of 79?
x: Kerala and Uttarakhand shared the top place with 79; Andhra Pradesh scored 74 and was 9th.

o: Centre for Economic and Social Studies, Hyderabad

s: Which of the following pairs about the present HDI method is correctly matched?
o: Education – adult literacy rate and gross enrolment
Combining the three indices – arithmetic mean
Income – GNI per capita (PPP), entered as a logarithm
x: Income is GNI per capita (PPP) in log form; since 2010 education uses mean and expected years of schooling and the indices are combined by a geometric mean.

s: Why are IHDI and district-level indices considered useful alongside the Human Development Index in assessing Andhra Pradesh?
o: Because HDI hides inequality within a State
Because district-level indices measure only population size
Because IHDI replaces all district-level data with national averages
Because HDI measures only infrastructure and excludes health
x: HDI can conceal inequalities within a State; therefore, the Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index and district-level indices provide a more differentiated assessment.

s: Since 2010, which method is used to combine the three HDI dimension indices?
x: Since 2010 the health, education and income indices are combined by a geometric mean.

s: Who conceived the Human Development Index?

s: In which year was the first Human Development Report published by the UNDP?
x: UNDP published the first Human Development Report in 1990, conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with Amartya Sen.

s: According to the National Human Development Report 2001, what was Andhra Pradesh's rank among the major States?

s: What was India's HDI in the sub-national HDI comparison of 2023?

s: The first Andhra Pradesh Human Development Report (2007) was sponsored by which of the following?
o: NITI Aayog and the World Bank
RBI and the Asian Development Bank

s: Which Aspirational District represents the lagging Rayalaseema belt of Andhra Pradesh?

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the lowest per capita income (GDDP)?

s: Among AP's 28 districts, which has the smallest population?

s: What Human Development Index target was set by the Sunrise AP Vision 2029?

Consider the following statements about Swarna Andhra @2047:

x: Swarna Andhra @2047 aims at a GSDP of USD 2.4 trillion, per capita income over USD 43,000 and 100% literacy.

s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25, what are the shares of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh's population, respectively?
x: Scheduled Castes account for 17.08% and Scheduled Tribes for 5.53% of Andhra Pradesh's population.

s: According to Census 2011, what was the Scheduled Caste population of Andhra Pradesh?

s: As per Census 2011, which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest share of Scheduled Castes?

s: As per Census 2011, Andhra Pradesh's SC population formed what share of India's SCs?
x: AP's 84.69 lakh SCs were 4.21% of India's SCs; 17.08% is the SC share of AP's own population.

s: What is Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva (formerly Aarogyasri)?
o: school assistance scheme of ₹15,000 per child
cashless healthcare scheme for 1.43 crore families
x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva provides cashless care to 1.43 crore families and covers 3,257 procedures.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Talliki Vandanam?
o: It is calculated per child, not per mother
It is the successor to Amma Vodi
It gives Rs 15,000 per child per year to the mother
x: Talliki Vandanam covers both government and private schools.

s: Which pair correctly gives Andhra Pradesh's MMR and IMR?
x: AP's MMR is 30 and IMR 19, so AP fares better on health than on literacy.

s: As per SRS 2016-20, what was the life expectancy of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's life expectancy was 70.6 years against India's 70.0 years.

s: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva provides cashless care to about how many families?
x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva covers 1.43 crore families for 3,257 procedures.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Cement manufacturing is a secondary-sector activity. Transport is tertiary, research and development is quaternary, and top decision-making is quinary.

s: By the nature of the activity, to which sector does mining belong, though GVA reporting places it in the Industry sector?
x: Mining is primary because it extracts resources from nature; in GVA reporting it is grouped under Industry.

s: Transport belongs to which sector of the economy?
x: Transport is a service, hence tertiary (APPSC 2018), not secondary.

s: To which sector does top decision-making by government and top executives belong?
x: Top decision-making is quinary ('gold collar'); research and development is quaternary.

s: Research and development belongs to which sector?
x: R&D, IT, education and consulting are knowledge activities of the quaternary sector.

s: Which of the following pairs represents the oldest primary activities?
x: Hunting and gathering are regarded as the oldest primary activities because they involve direct dependence on nature for subsistence.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an extractive industry?
x: Animal husbandry is a genetic industry because it involves breeding and rearing animals. Mining, capture fishing and lumbering take resources provided by nature and are extractive industries.

s: Animal husbandry is classified as which type of primary activity?
x: Animal husbandry breeds animals, so it is a genetic industry, not extractive.

s: Which sector accounted for the largest share of India’s GVA in 2024–25, on the new 2022–23 base?
x: The tertiary or services sector accounted for 52.9% of India’s GVA in 2024–25. The primary and secondary shares were 21.4% and 25.8% respectively.

s: Agriculture and allied activities contribute about what share of Andhra Pradesh's GVA?
x: Agriculture is about 33% of AP GVA against about 21% nationally, led by livestock and fisheries.

s: The new GDP series released in February 2026 is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: GDP levels 3–4% higher, manufacturing 21.4%, FY26 growth 6.2%
GDP levels 3–4% lower, manufacturing 14.7%, FY26 growth 7.6%
GDP levels unchanged, manufacturing 11%, FY26 growth 7.6%
GDP levels 3–4% lower, manufacturing 25.8%, FY26 growth 8.1%
x: The new GDP series placed GDP levels 3–4% lower, measured manufacturing at 14.7% of the economy and reported FY26 growth at 7.6%.

s: To which year was the base year of the GDP series moved?
x: The GDP base year was moved to 2022–23 in the new series released in February 2026.

s: Which new sector was added in the revision of the Index of Industrial Production mentioned in June 2026?
x: The revised IIP added a water supply and waste management sector. The other options are not the sector added in the cited revision.

s: In both India and Andhra Pradesh, which sector accounts for the largest share of employment?
x: Agriculture leads in employment, while services have the largest GVA share.

s: As per PLFS 2023-24, what was the primary sector's share of employment in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The primary sector employs 45.6% of AP's workers, though its GVA share is only about 33%.

s: Which sub-sectors lead agriculture in Andhra Pradesh, making the State more agrarian than India?
x: Agriculture is about 33% of AP's GVA against about 21% for India, led by livestock and fisheries.

s: About what share of India's workers is employed in agriculture (August 2026)?
x: Agriculture employs about 46.1% of India's workers, though services lead in GVA.

s: What does the term 'pink collar' refer to?
x: Pink collar means service jobs long held mostly by women; red collar is primary-sector outdoor work, blue collar manual work and white collar office work.

s: Workers in which of the following are called 'green collar' workers?
x: Green-collar work is associated with environmental protection and renewable energy. Office work is white collar, primary outdoor work red collar and top decision-making gold collar.

s: What does the term 'red collar' refer to?
x: Red collar refers to primary-sector outdoor workers; manual factory workers are blue collar.

s: In 2025, which country overtook Saudi Arabia as the top destination for Indian blue-collar workers?
x: In 2025 the UAE overtook Saudi Arabia as the top destination for Indian blue-collar workers.

s: Which collar colour refers to manual, factory and construction workers?
x: Blue-collar workers do manual, factory and construction work.

s: To which sector do 'gold collar' workers belong?
x: Gold collar means top decision-makers and experts, who form the quinary sector.

s: Which collar colour refers to office and professional service workers?
x: White collar workers are office and professional service workers; blue collar are manual workers.

s: According to the Fisher-Clark thesis, in which order do labour and output move during structural transformation?
x: The thesis states that as income rises, labour and output generally move from the primary sector to the secondary sector and then to the tertiary sector.

s: India’s experience of ‘premature deindustrialisation’ refers primarily to the fact that India
o: moved directly from agriculture to a large manufacturing base
skipped the mass factory-job stage to a considerable extent
x: Premature deindustrialisation indicates that India did not pass through a large mass factory-employment phase before the expansion of services.

s: Which of the following pairs about Andhra Pradesh's economy is correctly matched?
o: Manufacturing share of GSDP – about 33 per cent
x: AP is services-led with manufacturing at about 11 per cent of GSDP; Industrial Policy 4.0 for 2024-29 seeks to fill this manufacturing 'missing middle'.

s: Along with Allan Fisher, who is associated with the Fisher-Clark thesis?
x: The thesis comes from Allan Fisher (1935) and Colin Clark (1940).

s: Which policy targets Andhra Pradesh's 'missing middle' of low manufacturing (about 11% of GSDP)?
x: Industrial Policy 4.0 (2024-29) targets AP's missing manufacturing middle.

s: India accounts for only about what share of global manufacturing value added?
x: India has only 2.9% of global manufacturing value added, a sign of premature deindustrialisation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about global sectoral patterns?
o: In developed countries the quaternary and quinary sectors are shrinking
In developing countries the primary sector is still large in employment
In developing countries services grow faster than industry
Services form about 70-80 per cent of GDP in developed countries
x: The quaternary and quinary sectors are growing, not shrinking, in developed countries.

s: In developed countries, the services sector accounts for about what share of GDP?
x: Services make up about 70-80% of GDP in developed countries.

s: Which of the following is a feature of the unorganised sector?
x: Small scattered units, irregular pay and lack of social security mark the unorganised sector; public/private is a separate classification by ownership.

s: On what basis is the economy divided into public and private sectors?
x: Public vs private is split by ownership; organised vs unorganised by regulation.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the organised sector?
o: Coverage of labour laws such as PF
x: Absence of social security marks the unorganised sector; organised units are registered and follow labour laws.

s: As of January 2026, women formed what share of unorganised workers registered on e-Shram?
x: e-Shram had 31 crore+ unorganised workers, 54% of them women.

s: What is the share of informal employment in rural Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP informal employment is 62.3% in rural areas against 45.6% in urban areas.

s: About how many unorganised workers had registered on the e-Shram portal by January 2026?
x: Over 31 crore unorganised workers had registered on e-Shram, 54% of them women.

s: In which of the following crops does Andhra Pradesh rank first in India?
x: AP ranks first in oil palm and is India's largest fruit producer; podu cultivation persists in its agency tracts.

s: Which country leads the world in copper production?
x: Chile leads in copper; China leads in crude steel, Australia in iron ore and Brazil in coffee.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of diamonds by value?
x: Botswana leads by value, while Russia leads by volume.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of cocoa?
x: Cote d'Ivoire is 1st and Ghana 2nd in cocoa.

s: Which crop–leading producer pair is correctly matched?
x: China leads in tea; Brazil leads in coffee, the USA in maize and Thailand in natural rubber.

s: Which country was the world's largest exporter of tea by quantity in 2024?
x: In 2024 Kenya led tea exports by quantity and China by value.

s: Thailand is the world's leading producer of which of the following?
x: Thailand produces about one-third of the world's natural rubber (FAO 2024).

s: After Thailand, which countries are the leading producers of natural rubber?
x: FAO 2024 lists Thailand first, followed by Indonesia, Cote d'Ivoire and Vietnam.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of saffron?
x: Iran is the world's leading producer of saffron.

s: India is the world's leading producer of which of the following oilseeds?
x: India leads the world in castor seed production.

s: Which is the largest fishing ground of the world?
x: The North-West Pacific is the world's largest fishing ground.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of sugarcane?
x: Brazil leads the world in sugarcane (and coffee); India is 2nd.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of maize?
x: The USA is the world's leading maize producer.

s: Which State produces about 71% of India's coffee?
x: Karnataka produces about 71% of India's coffee; India is 7th in the world and AP 4th in India (Araku).

Consider the following statements about natural rubber in India:

2. India is the 2nd largest consumer of natural rubber.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India is 6th in producing and 2nd in consuming natural rubber, and Kerala gives 70-75% of the output.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about shifting cultivation?
o: It is found in high-rainfall forests of the Amazon, Tropical Africa, South-East Asia and North-East India
It is primitive subsistence, slash-and-burn agriculture
Forests are cleared by burning and cultivated temporarily with low technology
It is a capital-intensive, export-oriented commercial agriculture
x: Shifting cultivation is primitive subsistence farming, not capital-intensive export-oriented commercial agriculture.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Masole is the Congo name; Conuco is Venezuela, Ray Vietnam and Milpa Mexico.

s: What is shifting cultivation called in the agency tracts of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Podu (Penda) is the AP name; Dipa is Bastar, Bewar Madhya Pradesh and Jhum the North-East.

s: Where is 'Dipa' shifting cultivation practised?
x: Dipa is practised in Bastar and Andaman and Nicobar; Manipur has Pamlou, MP Bewar and the Western Ghats Kumari.

s: In which country is shifting cultivation called 'Roca'?
x: Roca is the Brazilian name; Milpa is Mexico and Conuco Venezuela.

s: Where is 'Ladang' the local name of shifting cultivation?
x: Ladang is used in Indonesia/Malaysia; Ray is Vietnam and Masole Central Africa.

s: In which region is shifting cultivation called 'Kumari'?
x: Kumari is the name of shifting cultivation in the Western Ghats.

s: What is shifting cultivation called in Manipur?
x: In Manipur shifting cultivation is called Pamlou.

s: In which State is shifting cultivation known as 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya'?
x: Bewar or Dahiya is the name of shifting cultivation in Madhya Pradesh.

s: Where did Arabica coffee originate?
x: Arabica originated in Ethiopia; Mocha, an Arabica, is named after the port of Mocha in Yemen.

s: To which species does Robusta coffee belong?
x: Robusta is Coffea canephora, a hardier lowland coffee of African origin.

s: Which coffee is named after a port in Yemen?
x: Mocha is an Arabica coffee named after the port of Mocha in Yemen.

s: Which organism caused the leaf rust that ruined Sri Lanka's coffee from 1869?
x: Coffee leaf rust is caused by the fungus Hemileia vastatrix; it wiped out Sri Lanka's coffee from 1869.

s: What is farming that applies high labour and capital input per unit of land called?
x: Intensive farming uses high input per unit of land; extensive farming uses large areas with low input.

s: Which of the following is livestock ranching?
x: Ranching is large-scale and commercial; nomadic herding involves seasonal migration for fodder and water.

s: What is farming over large areas with low input per unit of land called?
x: Extensive farming uses large areas with low input; intensive uses high labour and capital per unit of land.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about plantation agriculture?
o: Tea is associated with India and Sri Lanka.
Cocoa is associated with South Asia.
It is mainly practised in tropical regions.
x: Cocoa is linked with West Africa (Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana), not South Asia.

s: Mediterranean agriculture is practised in which of the following regions?
x: South-western Australia has a Mediterranean climate and Mediterranean farming. The Pampas are grain and ranching lands, New Zealand is dairy, and the eastern United States has mixed farming.

s: Which of the following pairs (type of farming – region) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Plantation farming – Malaysia, Brazil and India
Commercial grain farming – Prairies, Steppes, Pampas and Downs
x: Mixed farming is associated with north-west Europe and eastern North America; Monsoon Asia is the region of intensive subsistence farming.

s: Plantation agriculture, an export-oriented monoculture, is a product of which of the following?
x: Colonial estates were set up to grow one crop for export to the home country.

s: Which type of farming particularly requires refrigeration and transport?
x: Dairy farming needs refrigeration and transport; Mediterranean agriculture specialises in olives, grapes and citrus.

s: Which of the following is NOT a region of commercial grain farming?
x: The Prairies, Pampas and Steppes are grain regions; the Mediterranean Basin has Mediterranean farming.

s: Denmark, the Netherlands and New Zealand are noted for which type of farming?
x: Dairy farming is practised in north-western Europe, Denmark, the Netherlands, New Zealand, the US Midwest and south-eastern Australia.

s: Why does commercial grain farming have a high commodity (marketed) rate?
o: Dominance of wheat in the cropping pattern
Large mechanised farms and low local demand
Small plots worked by family labour
High rainfall in the growing season
x: Large mechanised farms and low local demand explain the high marketed share; wheat dominance is true but is not the reason.

s: What is the farming called in which crops are grown and livestock are reared on the same farm?
x: Mixed farming combines crops and livestock on one farm; mixed cropping is only sowing crop seeds together.

s: In which of the following regions is mixed farming mainly practised?
o: North-West Europe and eastern North America
x: Mixed farming is typical of NW Europe and eastern North America; it is not found in Monsoon Asia.

s: What is the use of grapes for wine-making called?
x: Viniculture is the wine-making use of grapes; viticulture is grape production itself.

s: What does apiculture refer to?
x: Apiculture is bee-keeping; pisciculture is fish rearing, sericulture silk and viticulture grapes.

s: What is reared in sericulture?
x: Sericulture is silk production; apiculture is bee-keeping and pisciculture fish rearing.

s:
Consider the following statements about hydroponics and aquaponics:
1. Hydroponics is soil-free cultivation.
2. Aquaponics combines hydroponics with fish rearing.
3. Both hydroponics and aquaponics are agroecological practices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Hydroponics is soil-free and aquaponics adds fish rearing, but neither is agroecological.

s: With which of the following does aquaponics combine hydroponics?
x: Aquaponics combines soil-free hydroponics with fish rearing; neither is an agroecological practice.

s: Which type of farming can grow crops year-round in stacked layers in non-tropical regions, even in harsh environments?
x: Vertical farming grows crops in stacked layers all year, is more efficient than land farming and works in harsh places.

s:
Consider the following statements about vertical farming:
1. It can produce crops year-round in non-tropical regions.
2. It is less efficient than land-based farming.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vertical farming gives year-round crops in non-tropical regions and is more efficient, not less, than land farming.

s: What is India's horticulture output, which now exceeds foodgrain output?
x: Horticulture output is about 362–367 million tonnes and has surpassed foodgrain output.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Integrated Pest Management — bio-pesticides, pheromone traps and natural predators
Natural farming — compulsory dependence on synthetic fertilisers and chemical pesticides
Organic farming — synthetic inputs and genetically modified organisms are avoided
x: Natural farming does not require compulsory dependence on synthetic fertilisers and chemical pesticides. Organic farming avoids synthetic inputs and GMOs, permaculture designs self-sustaining systems, and IPM combines biological and ecological controls.

s: Who pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)?
x: Subhash Palekar pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming. It is distinct from the broader organic-farming framework and from the Green Revolution breeding programme.

s: Which programme is described as the world's largest agro-ecological programme, covering about 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares?
x: APCNF (Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming) is the world's largest agro-ecological programme, with 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha. The National Mission on Natural Farming is the national mission (8.80 lakh ha), and IPM is a pest-control approach, not a programme of that size.

s: What has the United Nations designated 2026 as?
o: International Year of the Woman Farmer
International Year of Sustainable Rice Cultivation
x: The year 2026 has been identified as the UN International Year of the Woman Farmer.

s: Which farming system avoids synthetic inputs and GMOs, relying on crop rotation and manures?
x: Organic farming avoids synthetic inputs and GMOs and uses crop rotation and manures.

s: Bio-pesticides, pheromone traps and predators are tools of which of the following?
x: IPM relies on biological and ecological control such as bio-pesticides, pheromone traps and predators.

s: What does permaculture refer to?
x: Permaculture designs self-sustaining ecological systems; soil-free cultivation is hydroponics.

s: In which sectors did Andhra Pradesh sign an MoU with the Netherlands on 7 September 2020?
x: The 2020 MoU with the Netherlands covered food processing to help horticulture and aquaculture farmers.

s: Which was India's first fully organic State?
x: Sikkim became India's first fully organic State in 2016.

s: About how much area did the National Mission on Natural Farming cover by March 2026?
x: NMNF covered 8.80 lakh ha and 18.19 lakh farmers (March 2026).

s: In which of the following regions is nomadic herding NOT practised?
o: the Arabian Desert and parts of Rajasthan
x: The Amazon and Congo rainforests support shifting cultivation, not nomadic herding, which is found in dry or cold lands.

s: On what does intensive subsistence farming, which gives a high yield per hectare, mainly rely?
x: Intensive subsistence farming uses family labour on small holdings and produces high yields per hectare.

s: Which crop dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas?
x: Rice dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas; wheat takes over in drier parts.

s: Which was the core region of India's Green Revolution?
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
x: The core region was Punjab, Haryana and western UP; M.S. Swaminathan and C. Subramaniam were key Indian figures.

s: Who coined the term 'Green Revolution' in 1968?
x: William Gaud coined the term in 1968; Norman Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

s: Where is the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), which released IR8, located?
x: IRRI (1960) is at Los Banos, Philippines; CIMMYT in Mexico works on maize and wheat.

s: In which year was the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) founded?
x: IRRI was founded at Los Baños in 1960; 1968 is when Gaud coined 'Green Revolution'.

s: Which body was formed when CIMMYT joined ICAR in 2011?
x: CIMMYT (Mexico) and ICAR formed BISA in 2011, working in Punjab, MP and Bihar.

s: In which year did Norman Borlaug receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: Borlaug got the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970; the term Green Revolution was coined in 1968.

s: Where is the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT) located?
x: CIMMYT works on maize and wheat and is in Mexico; IRRI is in the Philippines.

s: In which year was the Borlaug Award for agricultural science started?
x: The Borlaug Award for agricultural science was started in 1972.

s: Oriental intensive farming is primarily associated with which of the following regions and characteristics?
o: The Mediterranean basin; winter rainfall and olives
The Prairies; mechanised wheat and high output per worker
The Pampas; extensive cattle ranching and low labour input
Monsoon Asia; wet paddy, high output per hectare and low output per worker
x: Oriental intensive farming belongs to monsoon Asia. It is characterised by wet-paddy cultivation, high output per hectare and relatively low output per worker.

s: In which season do regions of Mediterranean agriculture receive most of their rainfall?
x: Mediterranean regions get winter rain; viticulture, citrus and olives are typical.

s: Derwent Whittlesey's classification of world agricultural regions (1936) identified how many regions?
x: Whittlesey mapped 13 agricultural regions in 1936.

s: Who is associated with the crop-combination method of agricultural regionalisation introduced in 1954?
x: J. C. Weaver introduced the crop-combination method in 1954. Doi and Rafiullah subsequently modified the method.

s: Which of the following pairs (method – scholar) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Crop diversification – Bhatia, Jasbir Singh and Gibbs-Martin
